```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import math

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch import nn

text = open("data/shakespeare.txt").read()
chars = sorted(set(text))
n_chars = len(chars)
index = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(chars)}
ids = torch.tensor([index[ch] for ch in text])
n_train = 90_000
train_ids, val_ids = ids[:n_train], ids[n_train:]
print(n_chars, len(text))
print(text[:60])
```

The exercises use the text of the [language models chapter](language-models.qmd),
a local copy, [`data/shakespeare.txt`](data/shakespeare.txt),
of the first `r format(nchar(py$text), big.mark = ",")` characters of the [tiny Shakespeare text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/karpathy/char-rnn/master/data/tinyshakespeare/input.txt) [@karpathy2015charrnn].
`ids` numbers each of its `r py$n_chars` distinct characters by its place in the sorted list `chars`.
The first `r format(py$n_train, big.mark = ",")` characters are for training,
and the rest for validation.
